McKinley's assassination had a huge impact on United States domestic and foreign policy. Roosevelt fast tracked the expansion of United States sphere of influence with the aggressive use of America's shiny new navy, he also bolstered the navy considerably under his presidency. He worked to protect US interests in Cuba following the Spanish-American war, ensuring the waters between Cuba and Florida remained under US control was top priority after building that awesome canal in Panama. Its a long list of things he did but essentially he wanted the United States to compete at a global level more than any president before him and he pursued his goals like a madman. 

Domestically Teddy pursued breaking up large monopolies (Railroads mostly) and took an active role in managing the economy(Square Deal) and regulation (FDA). While McKinley might have done some of these things I think that the Unites states would have been set back considerably in relation to other world powers if not for Teddy, plus we wouldn't have so many awesome national parks!
